messages:
deploy-bot: Starting config-only deploy `cfg/route-limits/v2` to canary (10% traffic) in change window 02:00-04:00 UTC. Rolling out routing policy + batching tweaks. Please watch latency and errors.

sasha: Ack. I'll keep dashboards open (per-route latency + kvcache hitrate).

kevin: What exactly changed in the config? Can we get the snippet?

maria: Pasting the minimal change we pushed to the config service:
```json
{
  "routing_policy": "prefer-low-cost",
  "max_concurrent": 200,
  "request_timeout_ms": 2000,
  "batching": {
    "max_batch_tokens": 2048,
    "max_batch_latency_ms": 20
  },
  "prefix_cache_ttl_s": 30
}
```

leo: Noted. We're pinning model variants at the tenant layer, right? This is config-only for routing/batching.

maria: Correct — no model binary change. We did pin routing rules to `route-set-2026-03` so only traffic routing/limits changed.

deploy-bot: Canary reached target: 10% traffic. 4/4 canary hosts healthy. Metrics: throughput nominal.

oncall-bot: Observability: small uptick in p99 latency for route "chat-gen" (from 240ms -> 420ms) starting ~30s after rollout. Link: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/12345

leo: Seeing ~0.8% 503s on the canary percentile that correlate with kvcache misses + long tails.

kevin: Hmm. Hypothesis: batching latency window lowered to 20ms causes more small-batch flushes under bursty traffic -> more small requests hitting kvcache misses. Suggest revert batching window to 40ms for canary.

sasha: Agree. Also suggest temporarily drop max_concurrent to 120 to reduce head-of-line resource pressure while we root cause.

kevin: Plan: roll config back to previous safe set (max_concurrent=100, request_timeout_ms=1500, max_batch_latency_ms=40) for canary only, then iterate. I can trigger rollback.

maria: +1. Sanity check: does rolling back canary-only config require a full deploy or config service supports pin/override?

deploy-bot: rollback command: `/deploy config revert --id=cfg/route-limits/v2 --scope=canary --to=cfg/route-limits/v1 --reason="canary 99p latency spike"`

kevin: Executing rollback now.

deploy-bot: Rollback started at 1736004420 by kevin. Applying `cfg/route-limits/v1` to canary (10%).

oncall-bot: Alert: p99 latency trending down, 503 rate returning to baseline.

leo: Confirming 503s cleared on canary. Thanks.

maria: OK—closing the canary. We'll re-run a targeted test with an extended batch latency (40ms) and smaller max_concurrent, then try a staged ramp (10% -> 30% over 15m). Will add these to the release notes.

sasha: I've added a quick checklist to the release doc: https://docs.redwood/release-notes/route-limits-2026-03 ; includes rollback commands, monitoring queries, and heatmap to watch.

kevin: TL;DR: config-only change rolled back due to canary p99 spike. Next attempt: conservative batching window + lower concurrency, ramp slowly.

maria: Thanks team. We'll re-open a small canary after tests. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Thread closed (config rollback complete).
